title: Add trustworthy published-rate-equivalent cost estimates
description:
## Summary
Add published-rate-equivalent snapshot valuation while preserving the existing token aggregation byte-for-byte as a parallel path. Cost processing must operate on source records before lossy aggregation: raw record -> source semantic adapter -> BillableQuantity -> exact RateKey bucket -> strict rate lookup -> Decimal cost -> status/quality rollups. The backend is the sole source of arithmetic.

## Architecture
- PR0 freezes RawUsageRecord, BillableQuantity, RateKey, pricing-pack schema, cost_estimates schema, enums, fixtures, adapter files, registry slots, and CLI feature stubs.
- Parallel width 10 implements pricing loader, four source adapters, exact cost engine, JSON compatibility, dashboard, security harness, and built-in rate pack/docs.
- One integration owner connects shared files and registry.
- Three parallel verification tracks cover monetary/provider correctness, browser/security/compatibility, and docs/live/performance.
- One release gate applies all acceptance criteria.

## Success Criteria
- Existing token totals and legacy JSON remain unchanged when costs are disabled.
- Pricing never uses provider-level aggregate counters or implicit provider-wide fallback rates.
- Every priced quantity traces to exact provider/model/channel/variant/tier/context/meter/valuation dimensions.
- Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, and Cursor semantics live in separate adapters with record-level measurement quality.
- Decimal-string money, complete/partial/unpriced/disabled status, provenance SHA-256, and snapshot repricing are enforced.
- Strict data-only custom packs replace rather than merge defaults and are bounded against malformed/resource-hostile input.
- Untrusted labels cannot execute in the dashboard; no unauthenticated remote data exposure is introduced.
- Backend JSON and dashboard totals cannot diverge.
- Maximum workstream width is 10; graph is lint-clean and cycle-free.
acceptance_criteria: Raw token output is unchanged; costs are feature-gated; every priced value traces through a source adapter to an exact RateKey and Decimal rate; partial/unpriced/quality/provenance/security/compatibility rules pass; width is 10; all release-gate checks succeed.
close_reason: All children completed

title: PR0 contract gate: freeze valuation semantics and scaffold modules
description:
## Summary
Single-owner PR0. Freeze the semantic and security contract before any implementation branch starts. Preserve the current TokenAggregator unchanged and define a parallel UsageNormalizer path. Pre-create every module, adapter, registry slot, fixture directory, schema, and CLI flag stub required by downstream branches. No production cost behavior is enabled.

## Deliverables
- ADR covering published-rate-equivalent snapshot valuation, non-goals, static-dashboard/server boundary, distribution tradeoff, and immutable raw token accounting.
- RawUsageRecord and BillableQuantity interfaces with agent, provider, exact model, channel, variant, service tier, context band, occurred_at, meter, integer quantity, unit, record-level measurement_quality, semantics_version, and assumptions.
- Exact RateKey with provider/model/channel/variant/service_tier/context_band/meter/valuation_date/measurement_quality.
- Meters: input.uncached, input.cache_read, input.cache_write_5m, input.cache_write_1h, output; unsupported visible charges force partial status.
- Enums for complete/partial/unpriced/disabled, provider_reported/derived/estimated/mixed, and bounded diagnostic reason codes.
- Versioned pricing-pack schema and cost_estimates schema using decimal strings and explicit priced_subtotal_usd.
- Frozen synthetic backend and UI fixtures, legacy JSON golden, empty provider-adapter modules, central registry slots, and test directories.
- CLI stubs for --costs, --no-costs, --pricing, --require-complete-pricing, and --explain-costs; costs remain disabled by default for machine JSON.
- Safe-rendering contract: all labels untrusted, HTML-safe JSON serialization, safe DOM sinks, no frontend arithmetic.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Downstream workstreams have non-overlapping file ownership and compile/import against frozen interfaces.
- Negative OpenAI remainder is SEMANTICS_INCONSISTENT, never clamped.
- Anthropic aggregate unknown-TTL cache writes are unpriced unless an explicit assumption is attached.
- xAI context band requires request-level total prompt including cache.
- Cursor quality is record-level, not permanently estimated.
- Partial results have total_usd null and separate priced_subtotal_usd.
- USD-only, six-decimal half-up JSON, two-decimal display, snapshot valuation, and provenance rules are frozen.
- No production cost calculation or rate selection is enabled.
acceptance_criteria: ADR, frozen interfaces/schemas/enums/fixtures, empty adapter modules, registry slots, CLI stubs, security contract, and non-overlapping ownership exist; costs remain disabled; all downstream branches compile against PR0.
close_reason: PR0 contract/scaffolding accepted after two correction passes, 20 tests, strict schema validation, full-precision rounding regression, typed-interface checks, and independent adversarial PASS.

title: Integration: register adapters and connect end-to-end cost flow
description:
## Summary
Single integration owner after all parallel workstreams. Register adapters centrally, connect raw parser records to the unchanged TokenAggregator and parallel UsageNormalizer, route BillableQuantity buckets through the loader/engine/serializer, wire CLI flags, replace dashboard fixtures with backend JSON, and update only shared end-to-end snapshots. Do not redesign frozen contracts; failures return to the owning bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Data flow is raw record -> source adapter -> BillableQuantity -> exact RateKey bucket -> rate -> Decimal cost -> rollups, parallel to unchanged token aggregation.
- No provider branch edits the central registry outside this integration.
- --costs, --no-costs, --pricing, --require-complete-pricing, and --explain-costs work end to end.
- Backend is the sole arithmetic source and dashboard consumes emitted values.
- Built-in/custom provenance, partial states, diagnostics, and record-level quality survive serialization/rendering.
- Baseline token tests, adapter tests, JSON goldens, browser smoke, CSP/security checks, and performance baseline run.
acceptance_criteria: All ten workstreams integrate through the frozen registry and data flow; CLI, adapters, engine, serializer, dashboard, security baselines, compatibility, and performance work end to end without interface redesign.
notes:
Integration acceptance addition: costs-disabled legacy JSON/HTML must not call render_cost_dashboard or embed any cost dashboard fragment. Current output remains a local static file with no HTTP server. If any served path is introduced, apply costs.dashboard required headers, loopback binding, authentication for remote access, and no permissive CORS.
Review additions: pass all NormalizationResult.diagnostics into the engine and preserve details through serialization; do not reconstruct-only/drop adapter diagnostics. Raw Grok session aggregates use camelCase fields and remain unpriced without request scope. Generic Codex/ChatGPT/subscription channels must not match OpenAI API rate cards; only explicit API billing provenance sets channel=api. Costs-enabled zero visible usage serializes COMPLETE $0; costs disabled omits cost_estimates/dashboard entirely.
Integration contract gap to resolve centrally: Provider-mode hourly tooltips and monthly/yearly summaries require backend-produced rollups. Extend typed engine result, serializer/schema, and JSON with root and per-agent hourly (date/hour), daily, monthly (YYYY-MM), yearly (YYYY), and total rollups. Frontend may select/format these strings but must not sum or infer status. Add compatibility/schema/view tests. This shared cross-module change belongs only to Integration.
Verification correction: Codex total-only cumulative fallback must never clamp negative deltas. If any cumulative counter regresses or dimensions/model context change unexpectedly, preserve visible current/previous quantities and force the affected record/segment to SEMANTICS_INCONSISTENT unpriced before any partial positive delta can be billed. Add total-only cumulative regression tests.
Release cleanup: make root hourly_usage/daily_usage/monthly_usage/yearly_usage required in cost schema and remove obsolete compatibility allowance/tests; update executable help to four views and record-level Cursor/Composer quality; make global Ruff gate clean (imports, unused calendar, explicit subprocess check, aware now).
close_reason: Final release cleanup accepted: global Ruff, accurate help, mandatory root/per-agent rollup scopes, 124 tests, schemas, compile, costs-off byte identity, HTML/Node/XSS and diff gates pass.

title: Verify provider semantics, monetary invariants, and performance
description:
## Summary
Post-integration verification track 1. Exercise the integrated Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI, Cursor adapters plus Decimal engine with formula, model-mix, context-band, quality, status, property, mutation, large-count, and performance cases. Own verification tests and benchmark reports only; implementation defects return to their owning beads.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Anthropic uncached input and mixed 5m/1h writes, aggregate unknown TTL, OpenAI inclusive cache subtraction/negative remainder, xAI cached long-context threshold/missing band, Cursor variant/channel/reported-estimated quality, and reasoning-output inclusion are covered.
- Mixed models never collapse to provider fallback.
- Exact six-place totals, order independence, complete/partial invariants, raw-token immutability, and very large quantities pass.
- Costs-disabled performance stays within the PR0 regression budget; costs-enabled work scales with records plus distinct RateKeys.
acceptance_criteria: Integrated four-provider semantic matrix, exact monetary/property/mutation tests, model/context mixes, large values, raw immutability, and costs-disabled/enabled performance budgets pass.
close_reason: Provider/monetary/performance verification passed: Codex regression/reset semantics, 56 provider fixtures, Decimal/property/mutation/bounds, 123 tests, stable corpus and live 8,738-file measurements.

title: Verify pricing security, browser safety, and compatibility
description:
## Summary
Post-integration verification track 2. Run the adversarial pricing corpus and browser payload suite against the integrated product. Verify strict CLI validation, provenance, CSP/no-network behavior, safe rendering, status/quality UI, legacy JSON compatibility, and both dashboard modes. Own verification tests/reports only; implementation defects return to owning beads.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No XSS payload creates executable elements or handlers; no third-party request occurs; framing is blocked.
- If a server exists, loopback/no-store/no-referrer/nosniff/CSP/no permissive CORS requirements pass.
- Duplicate/prototype/oversized/deep/ambiguous pricing input is rejected with bounded diagnostics.
- Costs-disabled legacy JSON/token output remains unchanged; costs-enabled output adds only the versioned section.
- Complete, partial, unpriced, disabled, custom, estimated, and mixed UI states render without console errors.
acceptance_criteria: Integrated malicious pricing/browser corpus, CSP/no-network/framing or loopback-server boundary, safe UI states, CLI validation, provenance, legacy JSON, and both dashboard modes pass.
close_reason: Integrated pricing/browser/security/compatibility verification passed, including post-fix Codex regressions, 73 focused tests, Chrome/XSS/no-network, CLI/schema/provenance and costs-off gates.

title: Finalize provenance docs, live validation, and operator guidance
description:
## Summary
Post-integration verification track 3. Update README.md, AGENTS.md, ADR/operator docs, CLI examples, schemas, pricing update procedure, and non-goals. Validate built-in and custom packs on live histories without claiming historical spend or exposing private paths. Own documentation and live-validation report only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Published-rate equivalent, snapshot valuation date, not-an-invoice disclaimer, completeness/quality, priced subtotal, custom SHA-256, cache/model assumptions, and non-goals are clear.
- Users can run --costs, --pricing, --no-costs, --require-complete-pricing, and --explain-costs without reading source.
- Live JSON/dashboard generation passes both modes; remote exposure is absent or explicitly authenticated/loopback-safe.
- Built-in rate updates are reproducible reviewed data-only changes.
- Documentation matches emitted schema and --help exactly.
acceptance_criteria: Docs and live validation accurately cover published-rate snapshot basis, status/quality, provenance, CLI/explainability, cache/model assumptions, security boundary, non-goals, performance, and real emitted schema.
close_reason: Provenance docs/operator guidance/live validation passed and were refreshed after final Integration fix; 123 tests, schema, custom/default/no-cost, HTML/Node and live four-agent checks green.

title: Release gate: trustworthy cost-estimate acceptance
description:
## Summary
Final single-owner release gate after all three verification tracks. Run every revised acceptance criterion and close only when the feature is financially honest, reproducible, secure, compatible, explainable, and performant. Add no new feature scope; failures return to the owning bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Existing token totals are identical with costs enabled/disabled and legacy JSON is unchanged by default.
- Every priced amount traces to an exact model/meter RateKey with no implicit provider fallback.
- Four adapter suites, Decimal monetary tests, partial/unpriced rules, provenance, compatibility, property/mutation tests, XSS/pricing security corpus, browser modes, explain-costs, and performance budget pass.
- Dashboard arithmetic is backend-only and no unsafe remote exposure exists.
- Built-in pricing is data-only and custom packs are strict replacement.
- Beads lint/cycles pass and the epic is closure-eligible.
acceptance_criteria: Every revised acceptance criterion passes: token/JSON compatibility, exact RateKeys, four adapters, Decimal/status/provenance, strict packs, backend-only safe UI, diagnostics, security, explainability, performance, and Beads integrity.
close_reason: Final release acceptance PASS: 124 tests, Ruff, pycompile, schemas, costs-off compatibility, all CLI controls, provider semantics, Decimal/status/provenance, browser/XSS/CSP, live performance, docs claims and Beads integrity.

title: B1: Implement Anthropic billing-semantics adapter
description:
## Summary
Parallel workstream B1. Implement only the Anthropic UsageNormalizer adapter and its fixtures. Convert raw Claude usage into exact-model BillableQuantity records without changing raw parsers, TokenAggregator, other adapters, engine, registry, serializer, UI, or pricing data.

## Semantic Rules
- input_tokens is already uncached input; never subtract cache fields.
- Map cache_read_input_tokens to input.cache_read.
- Map detailed ephemeral_5m_input_tokens and ephemeral_1h_input_tokens to distinct cache-write meters, including when both occur in one request.
- Aggregate cache_creation_input_tokens with unknown TTL is unpriced unless an explicit frozen assumption permits estimated valuation.
- Preserve exact model, channel, variant/tier/context dimensions, output semantics, occurred_at, record-level quality, assumptions, and semantics_version.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Separate fixtures cover uncached input, reads, mixed 5m/1h writes, aggregate unknown TTL, missing model/channel, reasoning/output inclusion, and malformed counters.
- Unsupported or ambiguous quantities emit bounded diagnostics rather than guessed RateKeys.
- Raw token records and legacy token totals are unchanged.
- Adapter tests run independently and no central registry file is edited.
acceptance_criteria: Anthropic records normalize to exact billable meters without subtracting cache; mixed TTL writes and ambiguous aggregate writes are handled honestly; isolated tests pass.
close_reason: Anthropic adapter accepted after native nested cache TTL, malformed-record, unknown-TTL, and full-suite review gates.

title: B2: Implement OpenAI and Codex billing-semantics adapter
description:
## Summary
Parallel workstream B2. Implement only the OpenAI/Codex UsageNormalizer adapter and its fixtures. Convert raw usage with inclusive input counters into exact-model BillableQuantity records. Do not edit raw parsers, TokenAggregator, other adapters, engine, registry, serializer, UI, or pricing data.

## Semantic Rules
- ordinary input = total input - cached input - cache-write input for records using current inclusive semantics.
- Negative remainder is SEMANTICS_INCONSISTENT and the record is not priced; never clamp.
- Preserve cache-read and cache-write subsets as their own meters when supported.
- Preserve exact model, channel, variant, service tier, context band, occurred_at, quality, assumptions, and semantics_version.
- Reasoning tokens already included in output must never be added twice.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fixtures cover ordinary/cached/cache-write input, negative remainder, schema-version changes, reasoning output, exact model/tier/channel, unknown dimensions, and malformed counters.
- No implicit provider-wide fallback or guessed model is produced.
- Raw token records and legacy totals remain unchanged.
- Adapter tests run independently and no central registry is edited.
acceptance_criteria: OpenAI/Codex inclusive counters normalize without double charging; negative remainders are unpriced diagnostics; exact dimensions and isolated tests pass.
close_reason: OpenAI/Codex adapter accepted after inclusive subtraction, required counters, whole-record inconsistency, cache-write visibility, and review gates.

title: B3: Implement xAI and Grok context-aware billing adapter
description:
## Summary
Parallel workstream B3. Implement only the xAI/Grok UsageNormalizer adapter and fixtures. Preserve request-level total prompt information long enough to classify standard versus long-context pricing before aggregation. Do not edit raw parsers, TokenAggregator, other adapters, engine, registry, serializer, UI, or pricing data.

## Semantic Rules
- Context-band selection uses total request prompt tokens including cached tokens.
- After band classification, cached and uncached quantities remain separate meters with band-specific RateKeys.
- If request-level total prompt or exact model/tier needed for classification is absent, emit unpriced or explicitly assumed/estimated output; daily totals cannot reconstruct the band.
- Preserve channel, variant, service tier, occurred_at, record-level quality, assumptions, and semantics_version.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fixtures cover standard and long context with cache, threshold boundaries, missing request total, mixed model/tier, cached/uncached rates, reasoning/output, and malformed counters.
- Classification occurs before aggregation and no provider-wide fallback is emitted.
- Raw records and legacy token totals remain unchanged.
- Adapter tests run independently and no central registry is edited.
acceptance_criteria: xAI/Grok records retain request context for correct cached long-context classification; missing dimensions remain unpriced; isolated tests pass.
close_reason: xAI/Grok adapter accepted after exact-model thresholds, strict native shape dispatch, request-scope classification, aggregate malformed visibility, and review gates.

title: B4: Implement Cursor and Composer variant/channel adapter
description:
## Summary
Parallel workstream B4. Implement only the Cursor/Composer UsageNormalizer adapter and fixtures. Distinguish model/version, standard versus fast, Auto versus explicit selection, first-party versus third-party billing channel, platform-fee dimensions, and record-level reported/derived/estimated quality. Do not edit raw parsers, TokenAggregator, other adapters, engine, registry, serializer, UI, or pricing data.

## Semantic Rules
- Never classify all Composer usage as estimated; use the source record quality.
- Preserve reported Cloud Agents token components when available.
- Locally reconstructed transcript usage is estimated and carries explicit assumptions.
- Auto or unknown routed models are unpriced unless exact billable dimensions are reported.
- Cursor first-party, third-party, subscription-derived, model variant, and platform fee semantics remain distinct RateKeys.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fixtures cover Composer standard/fast, explicit/Auto, first/third-party, reported/derived/estimated sources, platform-fee visibility, unknown routed model, cache meters, and malformed counters.
- No model/channel inference produces a guessed complete cost.
- Raw records and legacy token totals remain unchanged.
- Adapter tests run independently and no central registry is edited.
acceptance_criteria: Cursor/Composer exact variants and channels normalize with record-level quality; unknown routing remains unpriced; isolated tests pass.
close_reason: Cursor/Composer adapter accepted after native run/team shapes, Auto routing, channel/quality, fee/cache-write visibility, single-role transcripts, and review gates.

title: G: Build reviewed data-only rate pack and operator docs
description:
## Summary
Parallel workstream G. Produce the reviewed built-in pricing pack and operator documentation as data-only artifacts. Use exact model identifiers and complete dimensions; never use regex, prefix, fuzzy, wildcard, implicit provider default, executable expression, runtime URL, or scraper. File ownership: built-in pricing data, pricing source manifest, and pricing/operator docs only; do not edit loader, adapters, engine, serializer, dashboard, or registry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- schema_version=1, USD, snapshot valuation date, exact model IDs, exact meters, decimal-string prices, and source citations are present.
- Duplicate/overlapping keys are absent and explicit zero is distinguishable from missing.
- Each card states channel, variant, service tier, context band, and pricing source date.
- Runtime fetching and historical-spend claims are excluded.
- Update procedure is a reviewed data-only change with fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed data-only built-in rate pack uses exact dimensions, decimal strings, source dates, no overlaps/fallbacks/executable rules, and has reproducible update documentation.
notes:
Planning sources to verify at implementation time:
- Anthropic prompt caching: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching
- OpenAI prompt caching: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching
- xAI documentation index: https://docs.x.ai/llms.txt
- Cursor Cloud Agents usage API: https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/api/endpoints
- Cursor Composer variants: https://cursor.com/changelog/composer-2-5
The committed rate pack must record exact consulted pages, assumptions, and valuation date; illustrative values from the review are not built-in prices.
close_reason: Reviewed data-only pricing pack/docs accepted with exact API channels, source provenance, exclusions, mandatory schema validation, and review gates.

title: C: Implement exact RateKey cost engine and status rollups
description:
## Summary
Parallel workstream C. Implement pure pricing over BillableQuantity buckets only. Aggregate nonnegative integer quantities by the complete frozen RateKey, resolve one unambiguous rate, multiply once per bucket using Python Decimal, sum at full precision, and serialize/display with frozen half-up rounding. File ownership: cost engine and engine unit fixtures only; do not edit raw parsers, provider adapters, loader, serializer, dashboard, registry, or built-in pricing data.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No float or JavaScript Number is a source of monetary truth.
- Order-independent bucket aggregation is O(records + distinct keys).
- Missing or ambiguous rates produce bounded unpriced diagnostics.
- complete/partial/unpriced/disabled and independent quality rollups match the schema.
- Partial total_usd is null while priced_subtotal_usd contains only the known lower bound.
- Quantities remain checked integers and raw usage is never mutated.
- Six-decimal JSON strings and two-decimal display helpers follow the frozen rounding policy.
acceptance_criteria: Pure Decimal engine aggregates integer BillableQuantity by exact RateKey, emits exact status/quality/diagnostics and six-place strings, never mutates raw usage, and passes isolated tests.
close_reason: Exact Decimal engine accepted with diagnostics preservation/bounds, full-precision rollups, exact RateKeys, enabled-empty semantics, and review gates.

title: E: Implement safe display-only cost dashboard
description:
## Summary
Parallel workstream E. Implement Provider-mode costs, statuses, quality badges, disclaimers, tooltips, and explainability drawer against the frozen cost_estimates fixture. The frontend formats backend values but never subtracts cache, selects rates, determines status, calculates totals, or re-sums rounded components. Treat every agent/provider/model/session/pricing label as untrusted. File ownership: dashboard HTML/CSS/JavaScript renderer and UI fixtures only; do not edit backend calculations, serializer, adapters, loader, registry, or pricing data.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Complete, partial, unpriced, disabled, provider-reported, derived, estimated, and mixed states render distinctly without relying on color alone.
- Partial displays say Priced subtotal and never present a bare total.
- Snapshot repricing date, custom/builtin provenance, hash, and not-an-invoice disclaimer persist.
- Safe sinks/encoding prevent script-breaking JSON, event handlers, SVG payloads, quotes, and Unicode separators from executing.
- Token Types mode remains unchanged; Provider mode supports all views and explainability without frontend arithmetic.
- Static output makes no third-party requests and cannot be framed; if any server path exists it is loopback-only by default with restrictive headers.
acceptance_criteria: Display-only dashboard renders complete/partial/unpriced/quality/provenance/explainability safely in all views, performs no pricing arithmetic, preserves Token Types mode, and resists XSS payloads.
notes: Review correction: current product boundary is a local static file with no server/network. costs.dashboard must export the mandatory header policy for any future served wrapper, but cannot claim a fragment enforces frame-ancestors. Integration must assert that costs-disabled/no cost_estimates output does not invoke or embed the cost dashboard; if a server is ever introduced it must apply the exported restrictive headers and bind loopback.
close_reason: Safe display-only dashboard accepted with valid states, XSS-safe rendering, restrictive served-header policy, honest static boundary, and review gates.

title: F: Build security, malformed-input, and property-test harness
description:
## Summary
Parallel workstream F. Build independent adversarial corpora and property tests from the frozen contracts. Cover stored DOM XSS, script-breaking JSON, prototype keys, duplicate JSON names, oversized/deep packs, decimal bombs, invalid counters, overflow/resource bounds, pricing provenance spoofing, and algebraic invariants. File ownership: security/property test modules, fuzz corpora, and fixtures only; do not edit product implementation or styling.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Payloads cover agent/provider/model/project/session/custom-pack IDs, warnings, legends, tooltips, and explainability.
- Pricing corpus rejects duplicate keys, unknown fields/version/currency/provider, numeric prices, negative/excess-scale rates, overlapping keys, prototype keys, regex/wildcards, size/depth/card/identifier limits, and non-UTF-8.
- Properties prove monotonicity, order independence, additive disjoint datasets, raw-token immutability, complete=>no unpriced, and partial=>null total.
- Mutation cases fail when Anthropic cache is subtracted, OpenAI cache is not subtracted, reasoning output is doubled, or invalid negatives are clamped.
- Tests allocate independently of token quantity and produce bounded diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Independent adversarial/property/mutation corpus covers pricing JSON, XSS, prototype pollution, resource bounds, numeric invariants, cache semantics, and bounded diagnostics without editing product code.
notes:
Security/interoperability references:
- RFC 8259 JSON interoperability and duplicate names: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259
- OWASP XSS Prevention: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
- OWASP Prototype Pollution Prevention: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Prototype_Pollution_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html
- OWASP CSP: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Content_Security_Policy_Cheat_Sheet.html
close_reason: Security/property/mutation harness accepted with adversarial corpora, bounded-resource and financial invariants, and review gates.

title: D: Implement feature-gated cost JSON serializer compatibility
description:
## Summary
Parallel workstream D. Implement the versioned cost_estimates serializer and legacy compatibility contract against frozen cost results. Costs are disabled by default for machine JSON; --costs adds only the new section. Emit monetary values as six-place decimal strings and statuses/quality/provenance exactly as frozen. File ownership: serializer, JSON schemas/goldens, and serializer tests only; do not edit dashboard, engine, adapters, loader, registry, or raw token aggregation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Costs disabled produces semantically and ideally byte-for-byte identical legacy JSON.
- Costs enabled emits schema_version, published_rate_equivalent_snapshot basis, valuation_as_of, pack id/kind/SHA-256, status, quality, total_usd, priced_subtotal_usd, per-agent daily data, unpriced components, and assumptions.
- Partial/unpriced/disabled semantics are exact and unknown fields are not invented.
- Custom provenance kind is application-owned, never trusted from the file.
- Strict schema and golden tests cover unknown-field consumers and legacy no-cost rendering.
acceptance_criteria: Costs-disabled legacy JSON remains unchanged; costs-enabled serializer emits only the strict versioned decimal-string schema with exact status, quality, provenance, diagnostics, assumptions, and goldens.
close_reason: Feature-gated serializer accepted with structural/application validation, disabled omission, enabled-empty regression, provenance, and review gates.

title: Specify provider cost UI contract
description:
## Summary
Wave 1 contract task. Define a static cost_estimates fixture and renderer expectations for the existing Token Types / Providers toggle before HTML implementation. Specify labels, currency formatting, unpriced states, disclaimer placement, Composer wording, and state preservation. File ownership: new docs/cost-ui-contract.md and test_provider_cost_ui.py only; do not edit claude-usage-calendar.py.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fixture covers priced, unpriced, zero-cost, and estimated providers.
- Every calendar view has explicit expected cost placement.
- Accessibility labels and color-independent text are defined.
- Token Types mode regression expectations are captured.
- No runtime source file is modified.
acceptance_criteria: Static fixture and renderer assertions freeze the provider-cost UI interface for all four views without editing runtime source.
close_reason: Superseded by claude-usage-calendar-cjn.1 PR0 contract/scaffolding gate from the revised plan.

title: Gate: freeze pricing, JSON, test, and UI interfaces
description:
## Summary
Recombination gate after Wave 1. Review the pricing catalog, executable vectors, JSON/docs contract, and UI contract together. Resolve naming or semantic disagreements before parallel implementation starts. This gate owns no implementation files; changes must be sent back to the originating contract bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Provider keys, rate names, cache semantics, rounding, null behavior, coverage, currency formatting, and JSON paths agree across all four artifacts.
- Runtime file ownership zones for Wave 2 are non-overlapping.
- Single-file distribution decision is recorded.
- Contract tests and UI fixture are sufficient for independent implementation.
- No unresolved interface questions remain.
acceptance_criteria: All Wave 1 artifacts agree and Wave 2 can proceed independently in three source ownership zones.
close_reason: Superseded by claude-usage-calendar-cjn.1 PR0 contract/scaffolding gate from the revised plan.

title: A: Implement strict immutable pricing-pack loader and CLI controls
description:
## Summary
Parallel workstream A. Implement strict, data-only pricing-pack parsing and startup-only CLI controls. A custom --pricing pack completely replaces the built-in pack and implies --costs. --no-costs skips loading entirely; combining it with --pricing is an error. Implement --require-complete-pricing and --explain-costs contracts without connecting provider adapters or dashboard. File ownership: pricing loader, CLI parsing/validation, loader fixtures/tests, and pricing provenance helper only; do not edit adapters, engine, serializer, dashboard, registry, or built-in data.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Read once at startup; no hot reload, recursive merge, expressions, regexes, interpolation, runtime fetch, or executable hooks.
- Reject duplicate names, unsupported version/currency, unknown fields/providers, non-string/negative/excess-scale prices, duplicate/overlapping rate keys, prototype keys, non-UTF-8, and configured size/depth/card/identifier/digit limits.
- Decimal strings parse without float; exact-byte SHA-256 is recorded; local path is never exposed.
- Application assigns builtin/custom provenance.
- --pricing/--costs/--no-costs/--require-complete-pricing/--explain-costs interactions and exit behavior match PR0.
acceptance_criteria: Strict startup-only replacement loader and all five CLI controls validate bounded UTF-8 data-only packs, exact Decimal prices, duplicate/unknown/prototype cases, provenance SHA-256, and documented exit behavior.
close_reason: Strict immutable pricing loader/CLI accepted with replacement semantics, bounds, duplicate/prototype rejection, valuation-date consistency, and review gates.

title: Price local agent usage at published API-equivalent rates
description:
## Summary
Make the cost dashboard fulfill its product goal: value supported Claude Code, Codex CLI, Grok CLI, and Composer local usage at explicit published API-equivalent rates instead of leaving all local channels unpriced. Preserve exact model/channel mappings and visible assumptions; never use a hidden provider fallback. Keep backend JSON at six decimals and dashboard display at two decimals.

## Success Criteria
- Reviewed 2026-08-29 pack includes explicit local-channel cards sourced from official providers/OpenRouter/Cursor.
- Supported local records map to exact priceable models/channels with assumptions and derived/estimated quality as appropriate.
- Large-history compaction preserves exact billable RateKeys and token totals rather than converting all usage to unpriced.
- Live dashboard shows nonzero provider costs where supported and honest partial/unpriced coverage elsewhere.
- Every displayed currency amount has exactly two decimals; JSON remains six decimals.
- Costs-off compatibility, security, schemas, tests, and live generation pass.
acceptance_criteria: Live local dashboard reports published API-equivalent costs with explicit mappings, exact token preservation, two-decimal UI, six-decimal JSON, and all compatibility/security gates.
close_reason: Published-rate-equivalent local costs shipped with exact mappings, honest partial coverage, and live dashboard verification

title: Snapshot OpenRouter and local-channel API-equivalent rate cards
description:
## Summary
Fetch the public OpenRouter model catalog and reviewed Cursor Composer 2.5 pricing, create a 2026-08-29 immutable built-in pack, and add explicit exact RateKey cards for supported local subscription/transcript channels. No runtime network dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exact cards cover supported Anthropic subscription models, Codex gpt-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna and existing supported models, Grok build aliases, and Composer 2.5 local transcript variant.
- Prices are converted exactly to USD per million-token decimal strings with URLs/date/provenance.
- Unsupported/unknown models remain unpriced; no wildcard/provider fallback.
- Loader default points to the new snapshot only during integration ownership or via a separately coordinated constant change.
- Schema/uniqueness/source tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed offline pack has exact explicit local-channel cards and reproducible OpenRouter/Cursor provenance with no fallback.
close_reason: Added reviewed 2026-08-29 built-in snapshot with 210 exact published/API-equivalent rate cards and strict validation

title: Preserve billable local usage through extraction and compaction
description:
## Summary
Implement explicit API-equivalent valuation mappings for local channels and change compaction to aggregate supported billable quantities by exact RateKey and hour instead of converting the entire history to unpriced. Extract Grok modelUsage models and assign explicit Composer 2.5 assumptions. Preserve unsupported coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Claude/Codex subscription records match only explicit subscription cards.
- Grok modelUsage entries split by exact model; aggregate standard-context API-equivalent valuation is marked derived with assumption.
- Composer local transcripts use explicit Composer 2.5 fast mapping and estimated quality assumption.
- Same-dimension streaming maxima remain priceable as derived estimates; dimension conflicts remain unpriced.
- Compaction preserves exact billable dimensions, integer totals, hourly scopes, and hard bounds.
- Live output has priced components/nonzero subtotal while unsupported records remain partial/unpriced.
acceptance_criteria: Local supported usage reaches exact rate cards and remains priceable through bounded compaction without hiding assumptions or unsupported usage.
close_reason: Local semantic adapters and compaction now preserve exact rate keys and produce nonzero live valuations

title: Format dashboard currency to exactly two decimals
description:
## Summary
Format all provider cards, tooltips, summaries, and explainability currency to exactly two decimal places such as $0.00. Use string-safe half-up formatting of backend six-decimal values; do not use floating point as monetary truth or change JSON precision.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every dashboard dollar amount matches $N.NN with carry-boundary tests.
- Backend JSON remains six-decimal strings.
- Complete/partial/unpriced wording and no-frontend-arithmetic contract remain intact.
- All views/modes and XSS/Node tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: All displayed currency uses exactly two decimals while backend JSON and financial semantics remain unchanged.
close_reason: Dashboard formats backend six-place decimal strings as exactly two visible USD decimals

title: Release gate: API-equivalent local costs and two-decimal UI
description:
## Summary
Integrate/review the pricing, extraction/compaction, and display work; regenerate the real dashboard and apply the complete quality/security/compatibility suite.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Live dashboard shows nonzero API-equivalent priced subtotal for supported local usage.
- Explicit mappings/provenance/assumptions are auditable and unsupported usage remains honest.
- Currency display is exactly two decimals, JSON six decimals.
- Full tests, Ruff, compile, schemas, costs-off identity, browser/XSS/Node, performance, Beads lint/cycles pass.
acceptance_criteria: All live, financial, UI, security, compatibility, and Beads gates pass.
close_reason: 128 tests, Ruff, py_compile, diff check, and live 600k-record dashboard regeneration passed

title: Cache parsed session records per file
description: Full scan reads ~7.7GB (31k JSONL files) and takes ~64s every run. Cache each file's parsed usage records keyed by path+size+mtime_ns so unchanged files are not re-parsed. Output must be byte-identical to an uncached run. Costs path (--costs) stays uncached for now.
close_reason: Closed

title: Keep usage history for deleted session files
description: Agents delete old session files (Claude lost everything before 2026-08-10; Grok before 2026-08-16). The parse cache currently prunes entries for missing files. Make it retain records from deleted files so usage history survives, move it to XDG data dir since it is no longer reproducible, and never silently discard it on script change or corruption.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cache cost-record extraction for --costs runs
description: Parse cache (lg4) covers usage records only. --costs still re-reads every session file via extract_cost_raw_records, so cost runs stay ~60s+. Extend caching to cost raw records (dataclasses, need lossless JSON round-trip).
notes: Since vx7, usage output includes records from deleted session files but --costs still only reads files on disk, so cost totals can undercount relative to usage totals. Caching cost records would also let costs keep deleted-file history.
